title: Sorting-bound external-memory weighted shortest paths
formal: Can exact single-source distances in an arbitrary undirected graph with nonnegative real edge lengths be computed in O(S(n+m)) external-memory I/Os independently of weight ratios?
definitions: Use the single-disk external-memory model with an internal store of M records and transfer blocks of B consecutive records, for all integers B≥1,M≥2B. One I/O reads or writes one block; all input reads, preprocessing transfers and output writes count. Records have a constant number of fields; vertex identifiers and pointers have O(log(n+m+2)) bits. Records and numeric fields are indivisible: no packing arbitrarily many labels or weights into one field, and no decoding such packed information by arithmetic. Internal comparison, copying, address calculation and permitted numeric arithmetic on resident fields are free, but internal storage remains M records. Use at most (n+m)^{O(1)} external records and a uniform deterministic algorithm knowing M,B. Let N=n+m and S(N)=max{1,N/B}·max{1,log_{M/B}(max{1,N/B})}; the max conventions include small inputs. The bound sought is O(S(N)) I/Os with an absolute constant for every permitted M,B, including M<n. Input is a contiguous vertex list and an arbitrarily ordered edge list for a simple undirected graph on [n], plus source s. Output is one record per vertex with its distance from s, using +∞ for unreachable vertices; no explicit list of every shortest path is required. Each weight is an atomic nonnegative real field. Exact addition and comparison of resident weights and distances are permitted, with every resulting scalar occupying one field; these fields cannot be used to encode discrete data into digits. Zero weights are permitted and there is no restriction on the ratio of positive weights. The output distance is the minimum sum of edge lengths along an s-to-v path, with the empty path of length zero for s. This is an exact-real record I/O model, not a bit-complexity claim for arbitrary real input. The required I/O constant is independent of all edge magnitudes.

context: Meyer and Zeh remove the weight-range dependence in earlier external shortest-path bounds, but their bound still has a term larger than sorting in relevant regimes.
why: The problem tests whether weighted graph exploration can be performed at sorting cost on external storage.
